source.author: ov
source.text: Ne tamen oblitis ad metam tendere longe exspatiemur equis, caelum et quodcumque sub illo est, immutat formas tellusque et quidquid in illa est: nos quoque, pars mundi, quoniam non corpora solum, verum etiam volucres animae sumus inque ferinas possumus ire domos pecudumque in corpora condi, corpora, quae possunt animas habuisse parentum aut fratrum aut aliquo iunctorum foedere nobis aut hominum certe, tuta esse et honesta sinamus neve Thyesteis cumulemus viscera mensis!
source.text_original: Ne tamen oblitis ad metam tendere longe / exspatiemur equis, caelum et quodcumque sub illo est, / immutat formas tellusque et quidquid in illa est: / nos quoque, pars mundi, quoniam non corpora solum, / verum etiam volucres animae sumus inque ferinas / possumus ire domos pecudumque in corpora condi, / corpora, quae possunt animas habuisse parentum / aut fratrum aut aliquo iunctorum foedere nobis / aut hominum certe, tuta esse et honesta sinamus / neve Thyesteis cumulemus viscera mensis!
source.text_english: But lest we, with our chariot-horses forgetting the goal, stray too far, let us know that the sky and everything beneath it, the earth and whatever is in it, changes its forms: we too, a part of the world, since we are not only bodies but also winged souls, and can go into the homes of wild beasts and be enclosed in the bodies of cattle, let us allow that the bodies which may have held the souls of our fathers or brothers or others joined to us by some bond, or at least of human beings, are safe and sacred, and let us not heap up our guts for Thyestes’ banquets!

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: inde meae quercus tripodesque animaeque parentum hanc pelago misere manum.
reuse.text_original: inde meae quercus tripodesque animaeque parentum / hanc pelago misere manum.
reuse.text_english: Then my oaks and the tripods and the spirits of my ancestors sent this hand to the sea.
